repo.name: spring-boot-realworld-example-app
repo.summary: RealWorld (Conduit) blogging backend built on Spring Boot, MyBatis and SQLite. It serves both REST and GraphQL (DGS) APIs for user registration and login with JWT, articles, comments, favorites, follows and tags. Clients are RealWorld frontends.

critical_flows.business_impact: All authenticated REST and GraphQL actions depend on this; a flaw enables impersonation or locks out every user.

Token with one part ignored; header lacking space yields anonymous

/graphql permitted at HTTP layer; resolvers throw AuthenticationException if anonymous

notes: E2 is a duplicate of E1 (same main method).
MyBatis XML mapper SQL and application.properties (jwt.secret, session time) are not in the skeleton but are critical for persistence and token security.
Flyway migrations define the schema and aren't visible here.
REST and GraphQL duplicate the auth and ownership checks. Divergence between them is a key risk.
Login password matching may be inline in UsersApi/UserMutation via the passwordEncoder bean (Sr4r6s).
Login password checks are duplicated in REST and GraphQL, so the two can drift apart.
Duplicate email, username and slug checks are check-then-insert, which is racy; there are no DB unique constraints visible.
The GraphQL createArticle path skips DuplicatedArticleValidator.
The distribution was heavily inflated by MyBatis declarations and delegating controllers; demoted to the pyramid.
